FAQ.title: Frequently asked questions
FAQ.description: The essentials on investment, timelines, and how we work with you.

one.question: How much does a project cost?
one.answer: It depends on scope. A prototype starts around $$$$, a full custom product around $$$$, and a continuous team runs about $$$$ per month. We give you a fixed number after the discovery call, not a range.

two.question: How long does a typical project take?
two.answer: A prototype ships in one to two weeks. A custom product is usually launch-ready in 8 to 12 weeks. Either way, you see working software in the first sprint, not just mockups.

three.question: What technologies do you work with?
three.answer: Mostly TypeScript across the stack: Next.js and React on the frontend, Node.js or Python on the backend, and Postgres for data. We pick the stack for your problem, not the other way around.

four.question: Who owns the code and IP after the project?
four.answer: You do, fully. Once the final invoice is paid, all code, designs, and assets transfer to you — no licensing fees, no vendor lock-in.

five.question: How do we communicate during the project?
five.answer: A shared Slack or Teams channel, weekly demos, and a live project board. You always know what shipped this week and what's next.

six.question: Do you offer support after launch?
six.answer: Yes. Every project includes a 30-day warranty period for fixes, and most clients move to a monthly retainer for ongoing work after that.

seven.question: How exactly do you use AI in your process?
seven.answer: AI pairs with our engineers for code generation, test coverage, and code review — it doesn't replace senior judgment on architecture or product decisions. It's why we ship faster without cutting corners.

AiPolicyPage.title: AI policy
AiPolicyPage.intro: We use AI as a tool for our engineers, not a replacement for their judgment.
AiPolicyPage.practice: In practice: AI helps us generate boilerplate code, write test coverage, and produce first drafts of components and documentation. Every line that ships is reviewed by a senior engineer before it reaches production — architecture decisions, security-sensitive code, and product tradeoffs are never delegated to AI alone.
AiPolicyPage.clientData: Client data: we do not use client code or confidential project information to train AI models. The code assistants we use operate under agreements that exclude training on customer data.
AiPolicyPage.updates: This policy may be updated as our tools and practices evolve.
